title: Prefractionating Cyanobacterial Extracts by Solid-Phase Extraction
author: Leonardo Santos de Jesus
materials: Use the IPA solutions to prefractionate the extract using the step-gradient shown in Table 1 . The total volume of 20 mL per fraction should be distributed in 2 test tubes (2x10mL). Table 1: Isopropanol (IPA) solutions for the fractionation method. * HPLC-grade water 100% Source: Authors (2023).

Solvents and solutions: Dichloromethane; Methanol (100%); HPLC-grade water; Acetone; Ethyl Acetate; Isopropanol (IPA):water solutions (20%, 40%, 70%, 90%, and 100% IPA). Resin: DIAION TM HP20SS. Equipment: SPE column with frits; Manifold and vaccum pump; 20 mL test tubes; Ultrasonic bath; 4 mL vials with caps; N 2 flow (eqquiped with glass microfiber polypropylene filter, 0.3 µm); Vacuum concentrator (optional).

steps.title: Prepare the Organic Extract
steps.instruction: Dissolve the weighed dry organic extract (previously prepared from a dichloromethane-methanol 1:1 solution) in the smallest possible amount of the same solvent in a vial, using an ultrasonic bath if necessary.

steps.title: Prepare the Dry Load
steps.instruction: Add an amount of HP20SS chromatographic resin equal to the mass of the initial dry extract to the vial and dry the mixture under a correctly regulated nitrogen (N2) flow to prevent the powdery resin from spreading.

steps.title: Set Up Vacuum Manifold
steps.instruction: Label 20-mL test tubes and place them in a rack inside the vacuum manifold.

steps.title: Pack the SPE Column
steps.instruction: Prepare the SPE column with HP20SS resin and frits.

substeps.instruction: Place one frit at the bottom of the SPE column (remove one of the two pre-existing frits if necessary).
Calculate the amount of resin: use a minimum of 1 g; if the dry extract is >0.2 mg, add 5-7 times the weight of the initial dry extract.

To prevent resin from sticking to walls, weigh the resin in a small cup made from a folded and taped weighing paper funnel; fit the cup upside down as deep as possible into the column using tweezers and release the resin at the bottom.
Tap the column a few times to ensure the resin is evenly arranged on the frit.
Place a second frit horizontally on top of the resin, using a glass tube to slowly push particles from the walls to the bottom for homogeneity.

steps.title: Equilibrate and Load Column
steps.instruction: Prepare the column for the sample load.

substeps.instruction: Equilibrate the packed column with 10 mL of HPLC-grade water (repeat 2x).
Connect the packed SPE column to the manifold and wash it with 10 mL of ethyl acetate and 10 mL of IPA.
Add the dry load to the SPE column using the weighing paper cup method.
Place a third frit on top of the dry load.

steps.title: Wash the Column
steps.instruction: After collecting the 6th fraction (F6), perform the final washes.

substeps.instruction: Wash the column with 2x10 mL of 100% ethyl acetate (7th fraction).
Wash the column with 2x10 mL of 100% acetone (8th fraction).

steps.title: Process and Store Fractions
steps.instruction: Dry, weigh, and resuspend the obtained fractions.

substeps.instruction: Dry the fractions under N2 flow or using a vacuum concentrator.
Transfer fractions to labeled, pre-weighed 4 mL vials (weigh vials without caps).
Dry the fractions again under N2 flow or using a vacuum concentrator.
Weigh the fraction vials (without caps) and calculate the prefractionation yield (%) as: (sum of fraction mass) / (mass of initial extract).
Resuspend the dry fractions using an ultrasonic bath with a small volume of HPLC-grade methanol or the solvent used to produce the fraction.
Fractions 7 and 8 (wash) may be stored together in a single 4 mL vial.
